# hohmann-button A button that waits in a parking orbit while its work is queued, then inks the transfer from Earth to Mars as the work is done. The craft meets Mars at 100% and the button says it is done. This is the button part of `hohmann-loader` and nothing else: the inline loader inside a real ` ``` The script puts the original's inline loader in front of the word: ``. You can write that span in the button yourself, as the original README does, and the button will use it. Until the script has started it the span is hidden, so without JS (or after `destroy()`) the browser's own progress bar never shows in the pill. Its `` stays the source of truth: with no `value` the craft waits in the parking orbit, and with a value the transfer is drawn to that share of its time. The button takes the `value` away only once a job has been quiet for 0.3 s (see States). ## Driving it A press starts it. The button goes busy and says its working word, and your code does the work and reports it. If the first report comes within 0.3 s, as upload progress does, the craft leaves straight from the still launch window; if not, it parks until it does: ```js const btn = document.getElementById('publish'); btn.addEventListener('hohmann-button:start', async () => { const hb = btn.hohmannButton; try { for await (const share of upload()) hb.progress(share); // 0..1 of the job: the transfer drawn that far hb.done(); // the craft finishes the transfer, meets Mars, and the button says "Published" } catch { hb.reset({ say: 'Could not publish' }); // back to rest at once, and the failure is said } }); ``` ```js import { hohmannButton } from './hohmann-button.js'; const hb = hohmannButton(btn, { working: 'Sending', done: 'Sent', reset: 2600 }); hb.start(); // busy, no value yet: the parking orbit after 0.3 s (a press does this for you). false if disabled hb.progress(0.4); // forwards only; 0 keeps it waiting (still, then in the parking orbit) hb.done(); // or done({ stay: true }) to keep the done word, done({ say: '3 more uploads' }) to announce that hb.reset(); // back to rest now, a fresh launch window (abandons a job: stop calling progress) hb.reset({ say: 'Could not send' }); // the same, and says why. A plain reset() mid-job clears the status line hb.state; // 'idle' | 'waiting' | 'working' | 'done' hb.loader; // the hohmann-loader controller underneath hb.destroy(); // removes everything it added; the button is its own markup again ``` Report in small, frequent steps, as progress events come: the drawing then keeps an even pace with the work. A big jump is eased in over about 0.3 s, and the planets hurry to catch up with it. `done()` with no progress before it is fine: the whole transfer is drawn, and the button passes through working on the way. After `destroy()` the controller does nothing. A late `progress()`, `done()` or `reset()` from a job that outlived the button is ignored, and a second `destroy()` is a no-op, even after the button has been set up again. ### Options (data attributes or the options object, which wins) | | default | | |---|---|---| | `data-working` | the word | the word while busy ("Publishing") | | `data-done` | the word | the word once the craft has arrived ("Published") | | `data-reset` | `2600` | ms showing the done word before it comes back to rest; `0` stays done until `reset()` | | `data-auto` | `true` | `false`: a press does not start it, so call `start()` yourself (after validating a form, say) | | `data-status` | none | the id of an element to speak through, in place of the status line the script adds after the button. Give it `role="status"`. If it has neither a role nor `aria-live`, the script adds `role="status"` and takes it off again in `destroy()`. Use it when the button may be removed, so its last word is said from an element that stays, or when the button's siblings must stay as they are (see Accessibility) | | `data-coast` | `6` | engine: seconds for Earth to go once round the parking orbit while waiting (Mars takes 1.9 times as long). The engine's own default, 2.6 s, reads as a spinner at button size; 6 s is a calm drift of about 60° a second | | `data-pace` | `1.25` | engine: the shortest time, in seconds, to draw the whole transfer. A quick job is drawn at this pace, so Earth sweeps its 255° of the transfer in 1.25 s. A larger value sweeps more calmly, and the done word comes later | | `data-fine` | `false` | engine: the engraved detail (Sun rays, hatched planets, ticks). It is drawn for a loader a few hundred px across. At button sizes it is too faint to read, so leave it off | Size is the class: `.hb-sm` 36px with a 22px orrery, the default 46px with 26px (the original's button), and `.hb-lg` 60px with 38px. The orrery sits concentric with the pill's round end. `.hb-solid` is the primary in ink, with the drawing in paper. `.hb-block` makes it fill its row. The pill hugs its resting word, so it is even at rest, and it never gets narrower than that: a shorter busy or done word ("Load more" to "Loading" to "Loaded") keeps the pill's size, set at the start next to the orrery, so the words that share a beginning cross-fade only where they differ. A longer word ("Send" to "Sending", "Publish" to "Publishing") grows the pill over 0.22 s: to the right in a left-aligned slot, to the left in a right-aligned one. Give it room to grow into if its neighbours must not move (the demo's editor footer puts Save draft at the other end). Keep the word short when the words around the button already say what it sends: a long resting word leaves a shorter busy word sitting in an empty pill. When the word changes, the old one fades out in 0.1 s, fast first, and the new one fades in over 0.2 s from 0.04 s, so the two only overlap while both are faint (they never read as one garbled word) and the cell is never empty. Theme with `--paper`, `--ink`, `--ink-2`, `--ink-3`, `--rule` and `--sans`. `--hb-paper` is the button's face and also the loader's paper, so set it to whatever is behind an outline button (the demo's cards set it to their sheet colour). `--hl-size` sets the orrery's size. ### Events (all bubble) | | when | |---|---| | `hohmann-button:start` | pressed (or `start()`): your cue to begin the work | | `hohmann-button:state` | every change, `detail: { state, from }`: idle, waiting, working, done, idle | | `hohmann:arrive` | from the engine: the craft has reached Mars | ### States | | the button | the drawing | |---|---|---| | idle | its word | the launch window: Earth, with the craft, and Mars 44.3° ahead of it, still | | pressed | the outline face sinks a pixel and darkens a touch; the ink face lifts a clear step instead, since near-black cannot darken much (the main mouse button, a touch, a held Space; under reduced motion the colour changes and nothing sinks). A mouse press slid off the button lets go of it, as releasing there does nothing, and slid back on it presses again | as at rest | | waiting | the working word, `aria-disabled` | for 0.3 s the launch window holds still, so a job that reports at once leaves straight from it. A job still quiet after that parks the craft: Earth with the craft, and Mars, going round at their true rates (Earth once in 6 s) | | working | the working word | the transfer inked from the launch window to the job's share of its time. From the parking orbit, the parking picture first cross-fades to a fresh launch window over 0.25 s: the Sun and the orbits stay put, the planets and the craft fade from their parked places into their launch places, and the ink starts at once. The icon never empties | | done | the done word | the craft on Mars. After `data-reset` ms, the same cross-fade to a fresh launch window | | disabled | grey word, faint edge, no hover and no press. The `disabled` attribute (or a disabled `
`), or your own `aria-disabled="true"`, at rest. A button disabled while its job runs keeps its busy and done look and goes grey when it comes back to rest | the launch window, in grey | At rest the drawing is part of the button: the still launch window. The original's button kept its loader hidden until it was pressed, so the drawing appearing (and the pill widening) was the press's first answer. ## Accessibility - A real `
